claims.text: Texas Tech's IMMS worked with Fort Worth based AVX Defense Technologies under the Army's FleetSpace program to develop the FleetSpace User Interface. The Army Aviation and Missile Command funds the program.
claims.quote: partnered with Fort Worth-based AVX Defense Technologies, under the U.S. Army’s FleetSpace program funded by the Army Aviation and Missile Command (AvMC), to develop the FleetSpace User Interface (FSUI), an integrated operations and maintenance platform
claims.document: Texas Tech Now, Texas Tech Spearheads U.S. Army Aircraft Resilience

claims.text: Texas Tech describes FSUI as a 3D interactive decision tool enabled by artificial intelligence, meant for Army aviation operation, maintenance and sustainment planning.
claims.quote: FSUI is a 3D-interactive, artificial intelligence-enabled decision-making tool based on digitization, analytics, integration and intuitive display of data from disparate sources, intended for the Army’s aviation operation, maintenance and sustainment planning.
claims.document: Texas Tech Now, Texas Tech Spearheads U.S. Army Aircraft Resilience

claims.text: Texas Tech researchers also built data fusion and flight operations algorithms and a predictive maintenance model driven by data.
claims.quote: Texas Tech researchers developed algorithms for data fusion and flight operations and a predictive, data-driven maintenance model.
claims.document: Texas Tech Now, Texas Tech Spearheads U.S. Army Aircraft Resilience

claims.text: The methods rely on neural networks.
claims.quote: The methods use neural networks, or simplified models of interconnected units that mimic the processing ability of the human brain
claims.document: Texas Tech Now, Texas Tech Spearheads U.S. Army Aircraft Resilience

claims.text: Researchers reported that in testing the networks predicted unplanned and 480 hour phase maintenance actions.
claims.quote: predicted unplanned and 480-hour phase maintenance actions, restored 37% of missing and corrupted flight data and reduced data volume by up to 30% and data files up to 73% in testing.
claims.document: Texas Tech Now, Texas Tech Spearheads U.S. Army Aircraft Resilience

claims.text: In testing the networks restored 37 percent of missing and corrupted flight data. They cut data volume by up to 30 percent and data files by up to 73 percent.
claims.quote: restored 37% of missing and corrupted flight data and reduced data volume by up to 30% and data files up to 73% in testing.
claims.document: Texas Tech Now, Texas Tech Spearheads U.S. Army Aircraft Resilience

claims.text: The Texas Tech team also built a tool called the Propulsion System Validator.
claims.quote: The Texas Tech team also produced a Propulsion System Validator (PSV).
claims.document: Texas Tech Now, Texas Tech Spearheads U.S. Army Aircraft Resilience

claims.text: Texas Tech says the Propulsion System Validator tracks the remaining useful life of aircraft engines on its own and recommends maintenance actions tied to the aviation technical manual.
claims.quote: autonomously tracking the remaining useful life of aircraft engines and recommending maintenance actions interlinked with the aviation technical manual
claims.document: Texas Tech Now, Texas Tech Spearheads U.S. Army Aircraft Resilience

claims.text: Texas Tech says both the FSUI and the PSV have been provided to the Army.
claims.quote: The FSUI and PSV have been provided to the Army, with FleetSpace demonstrated at the Army’s annual Experimental Demonstration Gateway Event and PSV at GE Aerospace
claims.document: Texas Tech Now, Texas Tech Spearheads U.S. Army Aircraft Resilience

claims.text: According to Texas Tech, FleetSpace was shown at the Army's annual Experimental Demonstration Gateway Event and the PSV was shown at GE Aerospace.
claims.quote: with FleetSpace demonstrated at the Army’s annual Experimental Demonstration Gateway Event and PSV at GE Aerospace
claims.document: Texas Tech Now, Texas Tech Spearheads U.S. Army Aircraft Resilience

claims.text: More than 18 undergraduate and graduate students worked on the project alongside Texas Tech researchers and faculty.
claims.quote: more than 18 undergraduate and graduate students contributed to the effort.
claims.document: Texas Tech Now, Texas Tech Spearheads U.S. Army Aircraft Resilience

claims.text: IMMS and AVX have worked together without a break since 2019.
claims.quote: IMMS and AVX have partnered continuously since 2019
claims.document: Texas Tech Now, Texas Tech Spearheads U.S. Army Aircraft Resilience

claims.text: IMMS postdoctoral research associate Henry Johnston said the techniques and models let maintenance teams find weak components, plan repairs ahead of failure and cut downtime.
claims.quote: allowing maintenance teams to identify weak components, schedule repairs proactively and reduce downtime
claims.document: Texas Tech Now, Texas Tech Spearheads U.S. Army Aircraft Resilience

claims.text: Johnston said these benefits will raise the availability of the Army aviation fleet.
claims.quote: All of these benefits will increase availability of the Army aviation fleet.
claims.document: Texas Tech Now, Texas Tech Spearheads U.S. Army Aircraft Resilience

claims.text: Aircraft maintenance professionals check aircraft systems with computer technology and hands on inspections.
claims.quote: Aircraft maintenance professionals use computer technology and hands-on inspections to assess aircraft systems and support operational readiness.
claims.document: Texas Tech Now, Texas Tech Spearheads U.S. Army Aircraft Resilience

claims.text: Helicopter systems hold complex mechanical parts that need regular inspection and maintenance.
claims.quote: Helicopter systems contain complex mechanical components that require regular inspection and maintenance to ensure reliable operation.
claims.document: Texas Tech Now, Texas Tech Spearheads U.S. Army Aircraft Resilience

claims.text: Co-principal investigator Tommy Dang said both technologies give soldiers capability to manage and operate their aviation fleets.
claims.quote: Both technologies provide great capability for soldiers to manage and operate their aviation fleets
claims.document: Texas Tech Now, Texas Tech Spearheads U.S. Army Aircraft Resilience

claims.text: Students finished three capstone projects during the effort.
claims.quote: Students completed three capstone projects over the course of the effort
claims.document: Texas Tech Now, Texas Tech Spearheads U.S. Army Aircraft Resilience

claims.text: Texas Tech presents the work as a step toward cutting the billions of dollars that civilian and defense agencies spend maintaining aircraft.
claims.quote: toward reducing the billions of dollars civilian and defense agencies spend on maintaining aircraft.
claims.document: Texas Tech Now, Texas Tech Spearheads U.S. Army Aircraft Resilience

claims.text: Texas Tech University and its Institute for Materials, Manufacturing and Sustainment are in Lubbock.
claims.quote: Texas Tech University, 2500 Broadway, Lubbock, TX 79409
claims.document: Texas Tech University, Institute for Materials, Manufacturing, and Sustainment (IMMS)

rejected.reason: AVX's site renders no readable body and the Army pages searched carry nothing on FleetSpace. Every claim rests on Texas Tech's own release.

rejected.finding: Any fleet service or operational result
rejected.reason: Every performance figure is stated in testing. No result from the tools in service is reported.

rejected.reason: The release names no aircraft type, unit or installation. The helicopter sentence is background.

rejected.reason: The release says only that they have been provided to the Army.

rejected.reason: None given. The 37 percent is flight data restored, not accuracy.

rejected.finding: Typical size of the data reductions
rejected.reason: 30 and 73 percent are ceilings ('up to'), not averages.

rejected.finding: A savings figure behind 'billions of dollars'
rejected.reason: The release puts no number on it and claims no savings from these tools.
